routes.description: Establish a cumulative inference to Christian theism by connecting a finite cosmic past, life-permitting physical conditions, the emergence of life, the character of biblical revelation, and a Christian account of suffering to a purposive creator.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the scientific considerations are shown to be more expected under purposive creation than under materialism, the biblical material remains credible as revelation, and suffering can be reconciled with the goodness and redemptive purposes attributed to the Christian God.

motionBridge.description: Show that the combined scientific, biblical, and moral considerations increase the comparative plausibility of the Christian God.

centralBridges.description: Connect evidence against an eternal past to a cosmic beginning for which a creator is an appropriate explanation.
Show that life-permitting parameters and the origin or complexity of life call for explanation and are expected under purposive agency.
Defend the Bible's theological and cosmological claims as compatible with its ancient genre and indicative of revelation rather than ordinary mythmaking.
Supply a coherent Christian account under which natural suffering and divine actions remain compatible with divine goodness and redemption.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Identify limits in materialist accounts of mind and the natural world's apparent order that can support the cumulative creator inference.

routes.description: Establish that the cited scientific phenomena do not warrant a creator inference and that biblical cosmology, natural suffering, and scriptural violence are more expected under human religious development than under an omniscient and benevolent Christian God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if cosmological and fine-tuning inferences remain underdetermined, naturalistic alternatives remain viable, biblical claims lack distinctive evidential authority, and suffering supplies independent evidence against the character attributed to the Christian God.

motionBridge.description: Show that the combined scientific, biblical, and suffering evidence does not increase, and may reduce, the comparative plausibility of the Christian God.

centralBridges.description: Show that current cosmology and arguments about infinity do not establish an absolute beginning or uniquely support creation.
Challenge fine-tuning and origin-of-life probability claims while preserving scientifically motivated or otherwise non-theistic explanations.
Show that biblical cosmology shares ancient motifs or errors and therefore lacks the distinctiveness expected from divine revelation.
Show that prehuman suffering, natural cruelty, and scriptural violence conflict with divine goodness and resist the proposed redemptive explanations.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Provide a physical account of consciousness and include both natural beauty and natural harm when assessing design-based inferences.

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning, Theorems, and an Eternal Past
sections.rationale: Whether cosmology, thermodynamics, physical finitude, and arguments about infinity establish an absolute beginning is a major premise connecting scientific evidence to a creator.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Naturalistic Alternatives, and the Origin of Life
sections.rationale: This section tests whether life-permitting parameters and biological origins favor purposive design or remain underdetermined because probabilities and non-theistic alternatives are unresolved.

sections.title: Biblical Cosmology, Genre, and Revelatory Credibility
sections.rationale: The evidential status of Genesis and other biblical claims bears directly on whether Scripture displays divine insight or the ordinary cosmology and literary forms of ancient cultures.

sections.title: Animal Suffering, Scriptural Violence, and Divine Goodness
sections.rationale: Prehuman suffering and biblical violence directly test the compatibility of the observed and scriptural worlds with the goodness, justice, and redemptive purposes attributed to the Christian God.

sections.title: Natural Order, Beauty, and Materialist Accounts of Mind
sections.rationale: Arguments from beauty, complexity, and consciousness provide supporting comparative evidence about purposive creation and the explanatory reach of physicalism, while remaining subsidiary to the named principal domains.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Thermodynamics, cosmic expansion, quantum mechanics, finite physical magnitudes, and mathematical objections to actual infinity converge against an eternal universe.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: The BGV theorem is claimed to exclude an infinite regress of earlier universes or Big Bangs, thereby supporting an eventual absolute beginning.

chunk-002:chunk002-c01.proposition: The extreme sensitivity of life-permitting physical parameters favors divine design because the proposed multiverse alternative lacks direct observation.

chunk-002:chunk002-c03.proposition: The unresolved emergence of life from nonliving matter and the immense informational complexity attributed to cellular DNA provide additional evidence of extraordinary fine-tuning.

chunk-002:chunk002-c05.proposition: The Bible's treatment of the sun and moon as created lights rather than deities, contrary to surrounding ancient beliefs, counts against its being mere legend.

chunk-002:chunk002-c07.proposition: The Bible should be read as theological instruction about God and humanity rather than as a comprehensive modern scientific treatise.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: Humanity left a separate paradisal world after Adam and Eve's revolt, and the present suffering world permits good deeds needed for redemption and return to paradise.

chunk-003:c003-08.proposition: Because God can restore life and grant eternal life whereas humans cannot, taking life can be permissible for God while remaining impermissible for humans.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-01.proposition: The world's beauty, complexity, and apparent intelligence provide substantial evidence for a creator while falling short of absolute proof.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-06.proposition: Materialism remains incomplete, and near-death experiences are presented as empirical evidence that some aspect of mind or spirit extends beyond matter.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: Big Bang singularity theorems do not establish an absolute beginning because they assume general relativity remains applicable where quantum effects become important.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: The BGV theorem establishes at most that inflation had a beginning, not that the universe as a whole had an absolute beginning.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Fine-tuning does not favor God when the probability distribution for physical constants is unknown and non-theistic explanations such as brute fact, multiverse, selection, and necessity remain available.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Genesis conflicts with established astronomy in its creation sequence, primordial water, timescale, and solid-sky description, making human composition a simpler explanation.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: Animal suffering across evolutionary history, biblical commands, alleged divine actions, and human-driven extinction is more expected if the Christian God does not exist.

chunk-002:chunk002-c02.proposition: Inflationary cosmology and the successful multiverse-based prediction of the cosmological constant give the multiverse more observable support than a divine fine-tuning explanation.

chunk-002:chunk002-c06.proposition: Biblical cosmology is not uniquely accurate because it personifies stars and depicts a solid heavenly firmament continuous with ordinary ancient cosmology.

chunk-003:c003-02.proposition: Hundreds of millions of years of animal suffering before humans contradict the claim that worldly suffering arose from human sin and supply evidence against God.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-04.proposition: Nature contains profound ugliness, predation, suffering, and mass extinction as well as beauty, so treating beauty alone as evidence of divine purpose is incomplete.

chunk-004:chunk004-candidate-05.proposition: Conscious experience plausibly arose through evolved bodily regulation, while brain-stimulation evidence strongly links phenomenal and emotional states to physical brain states.
